English:en.### Dificultades y rupturas: cuando el a: ### Difficulties and breakups: when love also purifies
English:en.**Amar no siempre es fácil.** \nTodo am:
**Loving is not always easy.**  
All true love goes through moments of testing, doubts, wounds or even breakups. But even there —in what hurts— there can be a call from God. Love, when authentic, not only makes us happy: it also purifies, teaches and transforms.
English:en.En el noviazgo surgen diferencias, decep:
In courtship differences, disappointments, weariness or fear of the future arise. Sometimes one feels not reciprocated as expected, or that the relationship has cooled. That is normal.  
Love is not a straight path, but a school where God teaches us to **love beyond ourselves**.
English:en.> “El amor no consiste en mirarse el uno:
"> “Love does not consist in gazing at each other, but in looking together in the same direction.”  
> —Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
English:en.Las dificultades pueden ser un espejo do: Difficulties can be a mirror where we discover our weaknesses, our selfishness or our wounds. Instead of fleeing from them, it is an opportunity to grow, to learn to forgive and to trust more in God.
English:en.### Cuando toca soltar: ### When it is time to let go
English:en.A veces, el amor también se purifica en:
Sometimes, love is also purified in **renunciation**. There are relationships that are not meant to continue, and discerning this with sincerity and prayer is also an act of love.  
Breaking up does not always mean failing: it can be the most honest and courageous way to love. God does not bless every relationship, but the one that leads us to holiness and to true self-giving.
English:en.**Soltar con paz** es reconocer que el o: **Letting go with peace** is recognizing that the other belongs to God before they belong to us, and that happiness is not measured by keeping, but by loving in freedom.
English:en.> “Amar es querer el bien del otro, aunq: "> “To love is to will the good of the other, even if that good does not include me.”
English:en.Después de una ruptura, pueden quedar he:
After a breakup, wounds, feelings of guilt or emptiness may remain. But the heart is not made to stay broken: **God can heal** what seemed lost.  
It is a time of silence, prayer and accompaniment. Of letting grace repair what human love could not.
English:en.Los sacramentos, la dirección espiritual: The sacraments, spiritual direction and friendship are medicine. The Eucharist sustains, confession frees, prayer consoles. It is not only about “turning the page”, but about **letting God write a new one**.
English:en.Las pruebas del amor no son un obstáculo: The trials of love are not an obstacle, but a purification. Mature love is born from pain embraced with faith. When it gives itself, forgives and learns, the heart expands and loves better.
English:en.Por eso, incluso las rupturas pueden ser: Therefore, even breakups can be part of the vocational path: they help to get to know oneself, to purify desires and to prepare to love like Christ, with truth and without fear.
English:en.* No tengas miedo de pedir ayuda: habl: *   Do not be afraid to ask for help: talking with a priest or a spiritual companion can clarify a lot.
English:en.* No idealices ni te encierres: el nov: *   Do not idealize or lock yourself away: Christian courtship is a path of freedom, not of dependence.
English:en.* No apagues la esperanza: si Dios ha: *   Do not extinguish hope: if God has permitted a wound, it is because He wants to bring forth a greater love from it.
English:en.La vocación es el compromiso profundo de: Vocation is the deep commitment to follow God's call. It requires effort and care to truly understand that call. This process of discovering God's will is known as **vocational discernment**.
English:en.El discernimiento adecuado implica vario: Proper discernment involves several key elements:
English:en.* **Profundo autoconocimiento:** compr: *   **Deep self-knowledge:** understanding your personality, your strengths and weaknesses, your inclinations, your spirituality, your mental capacities and even your physical health.
English:en.* **Un conocimiento sólido y un amor s: *   **A solid knowledge of and a sincere love for our Catholic faith.**
English:en.* **Familiaridad con las diferentes vo: *   **Familiarity with the different vocations**, what they entail and the way of life they shape in those who embrace them.
English:en.Naturalmente, este proceso no sucede de: Naturally, this process does not happen overnight. Vocational discernment is a **journey** that can take months or even years. It requires study, prayer and, above all, patience.
English:en.* El discernimiento **no es algo que s: *   Discernment **is not something that can be done alone**. The best way to discern is with the guidance of the Church, ideally accompanied by a priest or a trusted spiritual director who helps you discover where God may be calling you.
English:en.* Si buscas orientación —ya sea que te: *   If you seek guidance —whether you have simple questions or need deeper accompaniment—, **we are here to help you!**
English:en.El noviazgo como vocación y camino de en: Courtship as a vocation and a path of giving
English:en.### El noviazgo como vocación y camino d: ### Courtship as a vocation and a path of giving
English:en.**El noviazgo no es un paréntesis en la:
**Courtship is not a parenthesis in Christian life, but a true call to love as Christ.**  
Just as marriage is a vocation to unconditional giving, courtship is a time of discernment and maturation in love. It is the stage where two people get to know each other, discover one another and prepare to decide if they want to give themselves to each other forever.
English:en.### Un tiempo de discernimiento y gracia: ### A time of discernment and grace
English:en.Cada cristiano está llamado a la santida: Every Christian is called to holiness —including those who are engaged—. This time is not a pause, but an opportunity to grow in faith and virtue. Living courtship with God at the center means letting Him give meaning to the relationship: illuminating affections, purifying intentions and making love fruitful.
English:en.Cuando un amor te acerca más a Dios y te: When a love draws you closer to God and helps you love others better, there is a Christian courtship. The more engaged couples love each other, the more capable they are of loving God, and vice versa.
> “The heart was created to love. Let us therefore put Christ into all our loves.”
English:en.Amar no es solo sentir, sino aprender a: To love is not only to feel, but to learn to give of oneself. Courtship is a school of love where virtues are forged: respect, patience, generosity and fidelity. Small gestures —listening, yielding, waiting— prepare for a love that endures.
English:en.También es un tiempo para **formarse y c: It is also a time to **form and grow together**. Reading, dialoguing, sharing concerns about faith and marriage helps to build on rock. It is important to be accompanied, seek counsel and learn from those who have already walked this path.
English:en.Un amor auténtico cuida y respeta. La ca: Authentic love cares for and respects. Chastity is not a denial of love, but its protection. It teaches how to love without using, to wait to give oneself fully, to discover the beauty of the beloved person as a gift. Christian courtship is not measured by the intensity of desire, but by the depth of respect and the truth of commitment.
English:en.> Amar es ayudar al otro a ser santo, no: > To love is to help the other become holy, not to be an obstacle on their way to God.
English:en.El noviazgo también es tiempo de **amist: Courtship is also a time of friendship, laughter and shared life. It is not about isolating yourselves in the relationship, but about opening up together to the world: serving, doing apostolate, living the faith with joy. A Christian couple not only loves each other: they are a witness to God's love in the midst of the world.
English:en.Los novios que rezan juntos, que van a M: Couples who pray together, who go to Mass, who confess, who put God at the center, experience that their love becomes stronger and freer. In the sacraments one finds the grace to forgive one another, understand one another and grow in communion.
English:en.El noviazgo es, en definitiva, **una voc: Courtship is, ultimately, a vocation to true love, an invitation to learn to love as Christ loves his Church: with patience, with tenderness and with self-giving.
English:en.El papel de la familia y la comunidad: The role of the family and the community
English:en.### **El primer hogar de la vocación: la: ### The first home of the vocation: the family
English:en.Toda vocación comienza en casa. No en un:
Every vocation begins at home. Not in a seminary, nor in a convent, but in the warmth of a family that prays, loves and serves.  
There one learns to say “yes”, to look beyond oneself, to discover that life becomes great when it is given away.
English:en.* La familia es el **primer seminario: *   The family is the first seminary of the heart.
English:en.* Donde se enseña a **hablar con Dios: *   Where one is taught to speak with God naturally.
English:en.* Donde se aprende que la fe **no es t: *   Where one learns that faith is not theory, but shared life.
English:en.### **La comunidad: cuna donde crece la: ### The community: cradle where the call grows
English:en.Nadie discierne solo. \nLa **comunidad:
No one discerns alone.  
The parish community, the group, the movement, are places where faith becomes a living experience.  
There one discovers one’s gifts, shares concerns and finds concrete models of self-giving.
English:en.👉 La comunidad no sustituye la voz de Di:
👉 The community does not replace the voice of God, but it helps to recognize it.  
👉 It accompanies, encourages, supports… and prays.
English:en.> _Una comunidad que reza por las vocaci: "> _A community that prays for vocations makes them be born._
English:en.Necesitamos familias y comunidades que *:
We need families and communities that live their own vocation with joy, knowing that this already is a testimony.  
When a married couple lives united, when a priest serves with passion, when a religious sister smiles with faith, they are preaching with their life.
English:en.La vocación no es un tema del pasado ni:
Vocation is not a topic of the past nor only for “others”.  
It is the great adventure of every Christian: discovering how God wants to love the world through you.
English:en.🌾 **Padres, catequistas, sacerdotes, ami:
🌾 Parents, catechists, priests, friends…  
Let us speak of vocation naturally.  
Let us look at our young people with eyes of faith:
English:en.> “Este chico sería un buen sacerdote.”:
"> “That boy would make a good priest.”  
> “That girl has a big heart for serving.”
English:en.Y no solo lo pensemos: **recemos por ell:
And not only think it: let us pray for them.  
Every prayer is a seed in God's field.
English:en.Vive tu familia como Iglesia: ama, entre: Live your family as Church: love, give of yourselves and be a beacon of God's love in the world.
English:en.Cristo quiso nacer y crecer en la Sagrad: Christ wanted to be born and grow in the Holy Family of Joseph and Mary. From its origins, the family has been the first nucleus of Christian life, where faith is taught, lived and transmitted. Every believing home is a domestic Church, a place where the love of God is first preached through mutual self-giving and daily example.
English:en.Los padres son los **primeros predicador:
Parents are the first preachers of the faith. With their words and above all with their example, they teach their children to live in God.  
They foster vocations and help discover the personal call of each family member. Holiness is learned at home, in patience, forgiveness, work and daily prayer.
English:en.**Imagen sugerida:** Padres leyendo la B: **Suggested image:** Parents reading the Bible to their children, showing closeness and unity.
English:en.#### **Comunidad de fe, esperanza y cari: #### Community of faith, hope and charity
English:en.La familia cristiana es **una comunión d:
The Christian family is a communion of persons, reflecting the communion that exists in God between Father, Son and Holy Spirit.  
Through prayer, the sacraments and daily life, members exercise the baptismal priesthood, offering their lives as a sign of love and self-giving. Here one learns to be generous, patient and to love without reserves.
English:en.**Imagen sugerida:** Familia en oración: **Suggested image:** Family in joint prayer, in an attitude of recollection.
English:en.Como Dios crea y educa, la familia parti: As God creates and educates, the family participates in his work: to procreate, educate and form in love. Every home is an image of God, responsible for transmitting life, love and hope. The family’s mission begins by first preaching the love of God among its members, in daily self-giving and mutual care.
English:en.**Imagen sugerida:** Familia abrazada en: **Suggested image:** Family embracing in a natural landscape, reflecting love and creation.
English:en.#### Misión que ilumina el mundo: #### A mission that illuminates the world
English:en.Vivir la fe en familia no es solo cuidar: Living the faith in the family is not only caring for one’s own home, it is being a beacon for others. The everyday acts of love and service teach children and show those around us that the Christian life is true and beautiful. The family evangelizes by its example, its commitment and its self-giving.
English:en.**Imagen sugerida:** Familia participand: **Suggested image:** Family participating in parish activities or community service.
Family prayer unites and strengthens. Reading the Word of God, praying together and putting God at the center of daily life makes a difference in decisions, behaviors and emotional bonds.  
If the home revolves only around the worldly, the sacred dimension of life is lost. A family that prays remains united and transmits faith.
English:en.**Imagen sugerida:** Familia rezando ant: **Suggested image:** Family praying before a meal or at a commonplace moment of union.
English:en.La familia cristiana es **una Iglesia vi: The Christian family is a living Church present in the world, a reflection of God's love. Each member has the dignity and the responsibility to preach first with life and self-giving to the other. The home not only lives the faith, it radiates it; it forms, accompanies and evangelizes. Being a Christian family is a call to love without limits, to overcome selfishness and to live total self-giving, as God loves us.
English:en.**Imagen sugerida al final:** Collage de: **Suggested final image:** Collage of Christian families in prayer, celebrations and service, showing unity and diversity.
English:en.1. ¿Qué hace un sacerdote? \n El pr:
1.  What does a priest do?  
    The purpose of a priest is to lead people to Jesus and to bring Jesus to the people. He does this mainly by preaching the Word and offering the Sacrifice of the Mass.
English:en.Su vida diaria consiste en administrar l: His daily life consists in administering the sacraments —Baptism, Confirmation, Eucharist, Penance and Reconciliation, Anointing of the Sick and Matrimony (Holy Orders is administered by the bishop)— and in attending to the spiritual and human needs of his community.
English:en.2. ¿Qué es exactamente una “vocación”?:
2.  What exactly is a “vocation”?  
    A vocation is a call from God to do something specific for Him and for his Kingdom. The primary vocation of every person is to be holy: to love and serve God, obey his commandments and cooperate with Christ in the work of redemption by loving and serving others.
English:en.Pero todos somos llamados también a una: But we are all also called to a secondary vocation, a “state of life” in which we must be holy.
English:en.3. ¿Cuáles son esas “vocaciones secunda:
3.  What are those “secondary vocations” to which I might be called?  
    Many people are called to marriage, but it is a mistake to assume automatically that this is your vocation. You may also be called to the priesthood, to religious life as a brother or sister, or to the diaconate.
English:en.Finalmente, algunos siguen a Cristo en e: Finally, some follow Christ in the state of celibate life. Remember: it is normal to desire marriage and family. That desire does not exclude that you may have a priestly vocation.
English:en.4. ¿Cómo puedo saber a qué me llama Dio:
4.  How can I know what God is calling me to?  
    You should pray every day asking God to reveal His plan to you. Do not ask yourself: “What do I want to do when I grow up?”, but: “Jesus, what do You want me to do?”. And listen for the answer!
English:en.El lugar principal donde Dios habla es e: The primary place where God speaks is the heart. Listen with your heart. Also, the discernment of a priestly vocation is always done within the Church. The local bishop, assisted by the vocational office and the seminary, is the one who ultimately confirms the call.
English:en.5. ¿Puedo ser feliz si no sigo el plan:
5.  Can I be happy if I do not follow the plan God has for me?  
    If you do not follow the vocation for which you were created, you can attain some happiness in this life and still be saved, but you will never be as fully happy as if you followed your true vocation.
English:en.Por eso es tan importante discernir corr: That is why it is so important to discern correctly. Of course every vocation has trials and difficulties, but there is also great joy in giving your life for Jesus.
English:en.6. ¿Son felices la mayoría de los sacer:
6.  Are most priests happy in their vocation?  
    Most priests are very happy! Priestly life is deeply rewarding, both in this life and in the life to come.
English:en.Los medios de comunicación a veces dan u: The media sometimes give a distorted image of priests, presenting them as frustrated or unhappy, or reducing them to the scandals of a few. That simply is not true.
English:en.7. ¿Por qué los sacerdotes no pueden ca:
7.  Why can’t priests marry? Isn’t that very difficult?  
    Priests of the Roman Rite do not marry in order to dedicate themselves completely to Jesus and to His people. They beget “spiritual children” by bringing many souls to Christ and helping them grow in holiness.
English:en.El celibato es un signo poderoso para el: Celibacy is a powerful sign to the world that only Jesus can give us the happiness we all long for. Renouncing marriage and family shows that Christ is real and worthy of giving one’s life for Him.
English:en.Toda vocación exige sacrificios, pero ha: Every vocation demands sacrifices, but there is great joy in sacrificing for love. As one priest said: “It is true that no one will call me ‘dad,’ but thousands call me ‘father’.”
English:en.8. ¿Alguna vez se permitirá que los sac:
8.  Will priests ever be allowed to marry?  
    Celibacy will always exist in the Church because it is not only a law but a charism, a spiritual gift and a source of fruitfulness. Jesus was celibate. Saint Paul was too.
English:en.El celibato ayuda al sacerdote a unirse: Celibacy helps the priest to unite more intimately with Christ and to be a sign of the Kingdom of God. Although there are some married priests in the Catholic Church, they are exceptional cases.
English:en.Si alguna vez el Espíritu Santo quisiera: If the Holy Spirit ever wanted a change, He would effect it through the Pope and the bishops. But it would be a grave mistake to enter the seminary “hoping” that this will happen.
English:en.9. ¿Habría más sacerdotes si pudieran c:
9.  Would there be more priests if they could marry?  
    Maybe, but the question is whether that would be best for the Church. Celibacy for the sake of the Kingdom is a powerful testimony that Jesus is real and worthy of total self-giving.
English:en.Además, las vocaciones sacerdotales han: Moreover, priestly vocations have grown enormously in recent decades in Africa, Asia and Latin America, while they have declined in Europe and the United States. The problem is not celibacy, but deeper cultural and social factors.
English:en.10. ¿Estaré solo si me hago sacerdote?:
10.  Will I be lonely if I become a priest?  
    Loneliness is part of every vocation, but priests are rarely alone: they accompany people at the most important moments of their lives —birth, sacraments, marriage, death— and live surrounded by their community.
English:en.Cuando llega la soledad, Jesús llena ese: When loneliness comes, Jesus fills that emptiness, as He does in every vocation.
English:en.11. ¿Los sacerdotes reciben salario? \:
11.  Do priests receive a salary?  
    Yes, although they lead a simple life. They receive what is necessary to cover their expenses, maintain a vehicle, rest and carry out normal activities. In addition, the parish provides their lodging and food, so their expenses are minimal.
English:en.12. ¿Pueden divertirse los sacerdotes?:
12.  Can priests have fun?  
    Of course. Priests can practice sports, watch movies, read, travel, go to the theater, fish, play soccer or golf, as long as it is consistent with Christian life.
English:en.13. Si me atrae el sacerdocio, ¿signifi:
13.  If I am attracted to the priesthood, does that mean I have a vocation?  
    Possibly, but not necessarily. It is important to pray, attend Mass, live as a Christian and talk with a priest or the vocational director. They can help you discern clearly.
English:en.14. No soy muy “santo”. ¿Aun así puedo:
14.  I am not very “holy”. Can I still be a priest?  
    Yes. Holiness is a lifelong journey. God forms His priests little by little. Use the sacrament of Confession, pray daily and you will see how Christ transforms you.
English:en.15. ¿Es fácil llegar a ser sacerdote?:
15.  Is it easy to become a priest?  
    No. Serious formation is required: four years of college (including philosophy) and another four in the seminary to obtain the master’s in theology. But do not be discouraged: the seminary is a wonderful experience and God gives the necessary grace.
English:en.16. ¿Es necesaria tanta educación? \n:
16.  Is so much education necessary?  
    Yes. The priest must be well formed in the humanities, theology and spiritual life to serve with wisdom and be respected by the faithful. Every soul is precious and deserves a prepared pastor.
English:en.17. ¿Qué cualidades busca la Iglesia en:
17.  What qualities does the Church look for in a candidate?  
    He must be a practicing Catholic, who prays every day, lives the commandments, serves others, enjoys good physical, mental and emotional health, and has average or above-average intelligence. Above all, he must be open to the will of God.
English:en.18. Si entro al seminario “para probar”:
18.  If I enter the seminary “to try it out”, am I already committed for life?  
    No. The seminary is precisely the place to discern. Many men enter, test it for a while and then choose another path. And even so, they leave strengthened in their faith.
English:en.19. ¿Es interesante la vida del sacerdo:
19.  Is the life of a priest interesting?  
    Very much! Each day is different. There are challenges, but also a deep joy. At the end of the day, the priest can say: “Lord, today I have given myself for You”. There is no fuller way to live.
English:en.¿Responderás si Jesús te llama?: Will you respond if Jesus calls you?
English:en.## Dios no te hizo por casualidad: **te: ## God did not make you by chance: He dreamed you for something great. Your vocation is the unique way in which He wants to love you and for you to love Him.
English:en.**Atrévete a descubrirla… y a vivirla a: Dare to discover it… and to live it fully.
English:en.Pedir al dueño de la mies. Con rostros c: Ask the owner of the harvest. With concrete faces
English:en.Todos caminamos juntos y **lo que vivimo:
We all walk together and what we live of God is passed on.  
Observe who can continue the giving and encourage others to follow this path.
English:en.¿Dios me está llamando al sacerdocio?: Is God calling me to the priesthood?
English:en.¿Y si Dios me llama a darle todo?: What if God calls me to give Him everything?
English:en.¿Llevar a Cristo a todas las partes de l: To bring Christ to every part of society?
English:en.Ordenar todo a Cristo desde dentro: Order everything to Christ from within
English:en.## **¿Cómo saber si Dios me llama? — Ven: ## How to know if God is calling me? — Overcoming fear
English:en.Quizá alguna vez haya pasado por tu ment: Perhaps the idea of the priesthood has at times crossed your mind, but fear drives it away:
English:en.* Miedo al compromiso\n* Miedo al ce:
*   Fear of commitment
*   Fear of celibacy
*   Fear of not being worthy
English:en.Estos temores son muy comunes, incluso e: These fears are very common, even among those already in the seminary. But literally thousands of men have had the same doubts and yet became holy and devoted priests.
English:en.La primera verdad que debes recordar es: The first truth you must remember is that God does not speak through fear. Fear is a weapon of the Enemy to turn you away from God’s will; it is like the bite of an animal that paralyses its prey so it cannot move.
English:en.Un hombre dominado por el miedo tendrá d: A man dominated by fear will have difficulty advancing toward God’s will.
English:en.Entonces, ¿cómo superar el miedo? Aquí t: So, how to overcome fear? Here are five ideas:
English:en.Puedes tener preocupaciones legítimas so: You may have legitimate concerns about celibacy or preaching, but that is not the same as being afraid. Instead of letting fear dominate you, look at the demands of the priesthood objectively. It is true that a priest needs self-control, emotional maturity and the ability to speak in public. These and other areas require serious personal examination.
English:en.Sí, descubrirás cosas que debes mejorar,: Yes, you will discover things you must improve, but make your discernment with a calm mind, not with a frightened heart.
English:en.Recuerda que cuando Jesús llamó a Pedro: Remember that when Jesus called Peter (Lk 5:1-11), the first Pope said to him:
English:en.> “Apártate de mí, Señor, que soy un pec: > “Go away from me, Lord; I am a sinful man.”
English:en.Y Jesús le aseguró que no debía tener mi: And Jesus assured him that he should not be afraid to follow him. Likewise, Jesus knows your weaknesses and difficulties. If you trust in Him and “cast the nets into the deep,” everything will turn out well.
English:en.### **2) Reflexiona sobre el amor de Dio: ### **2) Reflect on the love of God.**
English:en.El P. Brett Brannen, en su libro _Salvar: Fr. Brett Brannen, in his book _Saving a Thousand Souls_, recommends this meditation when a man feels afraid:
English:en.> “Dios es infinito en poder y me ama in: > “God is infinite in power and loves me infinitely. No one can snatch me out of his hand. God will never send me where his grace cannot sustain me. If he asks something difficult of me, like becoming a priest, he will give me the grace to do it. I will not fail, because He is with me. I will be happy because I do his will. Even if I do not have all the necessary qualities, God will help me develop them. In his will is my peace.”
English:en.### **3) Confía tus miedos a la Virgen M: ### **3) Entrust your fears to the Virgin Mary.**
English:en.Recuerda que, después de que el ángel le: Remember that after the angel told her “do not be afraid,” Mary readily accepted God’s will:
English:en.> “He aquí la esclava del Señor; hágase: > “Behold the servant of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word.”
English:en.Entrégale tus temores a su intercesión:: Give your fears to her intercession: she will calm your heart and help you discover the will of her Son.
English:en.### **4) Recuerda para qué es el seminar: ### **4) Remember what the seminary is for.**
English:en.Desde un punto de vista práctico, es con: From a practical point of view, it is consoling to know that, if God calls you to the priesthood, ordination is still far off. The seminary is a time of intense formation to confront doubts, grow in holiness and prepare for fruitful ministry. **No man enters the seminary already ready to be a priest.**
English:en.### **5) Busca consuelo en la Palabra de: ### **5) Find consolation in the Word of God.**
English:en.Si tienes miedo al sacerdocio, no estás: If you are afraid of the priesthood, you are not alone. Prophets and apostles also felt fear when they were called. Read the following biblical passages to see how God encouraged them:
English:en.* **No soy lo bastante santo:** Is 6,1:
*   **I am not holy enough:** Is 6:1-9; Lk 5:1-11
*   **I fear failing:** Ex 14:10-31; Lk 15
*   **I have sinned:** Jn 21:15-23; Mt 9:9-13; Lk 7:36-50
*   **I am too young:** 1 Sam 3:1-18; 1 Sam 16:1-13; Jer 1:4-10; Lk 1:26-38
*   **I don’t have enough talent:** 1 Sam 17:32-51; Lk 1:26-38
*   **I want to have a family:** Gn 12:1-3; Mt 12:46-50; Mk 10:28-30
*   **I want “a good life”:** Mk 10:17-31; 1 Cor 2:9; Mt 13:44-46; Jn 10:10; Mt 16:24-27
*   **I’m afraid to commit forever:** Ruth 1:15-17; Mt 28:16-20; 1 Cor 12:5-10
*   **I am scared to speak in public:** Ex 4:10-17; Jer 1:4-10
*   **I am not smart enough:** 2 Cor 4:7-18; Ex 4:10-17
*   **I fear being alone:** Ex 3:4-22; Lk 1:28-38; Mt 28:20
*   **I want to be happy:** Ps 37:4; Mt 5:1-12; Jn 10:10; Mk 10:28-31; 1 Cor 2:9
*   **I am full of fear:** 1 Jn 4:18 “There is no fear in love; perfect love casts out fear.”
English:en.Como recordaba con frecuencia san Juan P: As St. John Paul II frequently reminded: **Do not be afraid!** Do not let fear paralyze you. Talk with a priest you trust about your concerns.
English:en.Permanece fiel a la oración diaria, conf: Remain faithful to daily prayer, trust in God and your heart will be at peace, whatever your vocation may be.
English:en.## **Ministerios laicales: La Iglesia cu: ## **Lay ministries: The Church counts on you**
English:en.### **Todos estamos llamados. Todos pode: ### **We are all called. We can all serve.**
English:en.La misión de la Iglesia no es sólo de lo: The mission of the Church is not only for priests. Every baptized faithful has a unique place in the history of salvation. Through their faith, dedication and commitment, the laity participate in Christ’s mission: **priestly, prophetic and kingly**, each according to their gifts and circumstances.
English:en.Ser laico no significa ser espectador. S: Being lay does not mean being a spectator. It means **taking the faith and living it in daily life**. The laity are called to act as **light in the world**, transforming, **from the spirit of Christ**,
English:en.* Sobre todo, la vida familiar y profe: *   Above all, family and professional life.
English:en.> Cuantos más laicos compenetrados con e: "> The more laypeople imbued with the evangelical spirit there are, the more the world will open to the Kingdom of God.
English:en.Los laicos pueden participar directament: Laypeople can participate directly in the life of the Church in many ways. **It is not necessary to be a priest** to contribute to the liturgy or pastoral care, always under the guidance of the pastors.
English:en.* Proclamar la Palabra de Dios en la e: *   Proclaim the Word of God at the Eucharist
English:en.* Dar la Sagrada Comunión cuando los m: *   Give Holy Communion when ministers cannot
English:en.Estas tareas, aunque importantes, **no h: These tasks, although important, **do not make the layperson a priest**. Their legitimacy comes from pastoral authority and their **sacramental root is Baptism and Confirmation**, not ordination.
English:en.<p style=\"text-align: center\">Cada lec: Every lector, Communion minister, catechist or participant in any lay ministry not only performs a function, but is called to be holy in their service.
English:en.La verdadera eficacia de su labor no dep: The true effectiveness of their work does not depend solely on technique or formal compliance, but on a **life given and coherent with the faith**. Being a lector or catechist implies preparing the heart, cultivating prayer and living the Gospel so that every word, every gesture and every encounter **transmits the presence of Christ**.
English:en.<p style=\"text-align: center\">El minis: The lay ministry thus becomes a path of personal sanctification: it is not enough to transmit knowledge, distribute the Eucharist or guide catechesis if one does not first live one’s faith with authenticity.
English:en.La santidad del laico transforma su mini: The holiness of the layperson transforms their ministry, making it a light for others and true support for priests. Every act of service, however small it may seem, **is a living testimony of God’s love** and an example that inspires the whole community.
English:en.> Ser laico que sirve es ser santo en lo: > Being a layperson who serves is being holy in the ordinary, reflecting the Gospel not only in function, but in every aspect of life.
English:en.### **La vocación no nace de la nada**: ### **A vocation does not arise from nothing**
English:en.A veces parece que las vocaciones —al sa:
Sometimes it seems that vocations — to the priesthood, to marriage, or to consecrated life — **arise from nothing**, as if God called in secret without anyone else being involved.  
But that is not the case: **God calls through concrete faces, through living communities, through people who truly care.**  
Therefore, it is not enough to pray for vocations. **You must seek them.**
English:en.Jesús lo dijo con claridad: _“La mies es:
Jesus said it clearly: _“The harvest is abundant and the laborers are few; therefore pray to the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest”_ (Mt 9:37-38).  
That prayer is not passive or theoretical. It is a call to **become collaborators of God ourselves**, to help others discover their path.
English:en.Rezar por las vocaciones significa **mir:
Praying for vocations means **looking around**: at the young people in your parish, at your friends, at those who serve with joy, at those who listen with patience, at those who live the faith coherently.  
When you see someone like that, **do not stay silent**. It may be time to ask, with simplicity and confidence:
English:en.> “¿Has pensado alguna vez que Dios podr: "> “Have you ever thought that God might be calling you to something more?”
English:en.A veces una pregunta como esa, lanzada p: Sometimes a question like that, asked by a **priest**, a **catechist**, or a **believing friend**, can awaken a sleeping vocation.
English:en.### **Cada uno busca la santidad del otr: ### **Each one seeks the holiness of the other**
English:en.La vocación no es un asunto privado. **T:
Vocation is not a private matter. **We are all responsible for the holiness of others.**  
A layperson who encourages, a mother who prays, a priest who proposes, a community that accompanies… all take part in the birth of new vocations.
English:en.El mundo necesita **buenos esposos**, **: The world needs **good husbands**, **good priests**, **good consecrated women**. And that begins when someone dares to look with faith at another’s qualities:
English:en.> “Sería un padre entregado.” \n> “Podr:
"> “He would be a devoted father.”  
> “She could be a great sister.”  
> “He has the soul of a shepherd.”
English:en.No se trata de etiquetar, sino de **reco: It is not about labeling, but about **recognizing God’s action** in people and helping them discern it.
English:en.Mira con atención. **Apunta en el corazó:
Look attentively. **Write in your heart** the names of those who convey joy, hope, service.  
Accompany them with your friendship, with your prayer, with your example.  
And pray each day:
English:en.> “Señor, haz que cada uno descubra su c: "> “Lord, help each person discover their path, and help us accompany one another in discernment.”
English:en.Ninguna vocación florece en solitario. *:
No vocation flourishes alone. **It arises in a community that prays, that listens, that walks united.**  
Synodality — that walking together — is not just a pastoral method: **it is the very way God calls**.  
Every vocation, every story, is the fruit of a people who accompany, propose, and sustain.
English:en.Noviazgo y Seminario. Épocas de discerni: Courtship and Seminary. Times of discernment
English:en.Pedid al dueño de la mies: Ask the owner of the harvest
English:en.Jesús lo dijo con verdad: **hay mucho tr:
Jesus said it truthfully: **there is much work to do and few hands willing to do it.**  
Souls — that is the harvest — **await shepherds to accompany them, to heal them, to lead them toward God.**  
But if priests are lacking, **there are no ones to carry the Gospel, to celebrate the sacraments, to announce Christ’s forgiveness and mercy.**
English:en.No se trata solo de una escasez numérica:
It is not only a numerical shortage: it is an **urgency at the heart of the Church.**  
There is hunger for God, thirst for meaning, need for shepherds.  
And Christ himself told us how to respond: **by asking.**
English:en.Jesús no dijo “organizad más” o “buscad: Jesus did not say “organize more” or “seek better methods.” He said:
English:en.> **“Rogad al Dueño de la mies.”**: "> **“Pray to the Lord of the harvest.”**
English:en.La vocación sacerdotal **no nace de una:
Priestly vocation **does not arise from a strategy, but from prayer.**  
God continues to call, but **waits for his people to intercede.**  
When the Church prays, the Holy Spirit acts; when a family prays, a heart can hear the call.
English:en.Por eso, **cada cristiano tiene una resp:
Therefore, **every Christian has a real responsibility:**  
**to ask the Lord of the harvest to send holy, generous, joyful laborers.**
English:en.No basta con pedir una vez. Jesús habló:
It is not enough to ask once. Jesus spoke of **praying without ceasing.**  
Priestly vocations are born in a Church that **prays with persistence and trust.**
English:en.Reza cada día, reza en familia, reza el:
Pray each day, pray as a family, pray the Rosary asking for priests and for those who could be one.  
**Each Hail Mary is a seed.**  
And how many priests, when recounting their story, confess it:
English:en.> “Mi abuela rezaba el Rosario por las v:
"> “My grandmother prayed the Rosary for vocations.”  
> “A group in my parish prayed each week for new priests.”  
> “Someone, in silence, was praying for me.”
English:en.**Nada se pierde.** Cada oración mueve e: **Nothing is lost.** Every prayer moves the heart of God.
English:en.Pedir vocaciones es un acto de fe, pero:
Asking for vocations is an act of faith, but also of generosity.  
It means recognizing that **the Church does not belong to us**: it belongs to Christ.  
And He wants his harvest to have laborers, his people to have shepherds.
English:en.Dedicar tiempo, oración, sacrificio, inc:
Dedicating time, prayer, sacrifice, even offering a Rosary or a communion for vocations, **is part of our mission as laity, families, and communities.**  
There is no prayer more fruitful than one that asks for those who will one day **bring God’s grace to so many souls.**
English:en.La vocación nace en una **comunidad que:
Vocation is born in a **community that prays**, that walks united, that lives the **synodality** of being responsible for everyone.  
It is not enough to wait for “others” to pray.  
**Everyone counts.** Each one can be an instrument so that a young person hears the voice of Christ calling:
English:en.La mies es mucha. Las almas esperan. \n:
The harvest is plentiful. Souls are waiting.  
And the Lord has given us the way: **ask, trust, insist.**
English:en.Pide cada día al Dueño de la mies. \nHa:
Ask each day to the Lord of the harvest.  
Do it with faith, with constancy, with love for the Church.  
Because God listens. And when the Church prays, **He answers.**
English:en.### Dos caminos, una misma entrega: la v: ### Two paths, one same surrender: active life and contemplative life
English:en.Cuando alguien pregunta _“¿qué hacen las:
When someone asks _“what do nuns do?”_, the most honest answer would be:  
**“they love, serve, and pray for the world”**.  
But behind those three words there is **a whole life of devotion**.  
Some do it **in silence, within walls**, and others **in the midst of the noise of the world**.  
Both forms are two faces of the same love: **Christ**.
English:en.> “Las monjas son el rostro femenino de: "> “Nuns are the feminine face of a Church that prays, serves, and loves.”
English:en.## Monjas de clausura: el corazón oculto: ## Cloistered nuns: the hidden heart that sustains everyone
English:en.Son las **monjas contemplativas**, las q:
They are the **contemplative nuns**, those who live “hidden with Christ in God.”  
From the silence of their monasteries, **they pray for everyone**, for believers and nonbelievers, for those who suffer, for those who love, for the whole world.
English:en.### Así late su día: ### This is how their day beats
English:en.Su vida está marcada por un ritmo sereno: Their life is marked by a serene, steady rhythm:
English:en.* **Silencio**, que no es vacío, sino: *   **Silence**, which is not emptiness but an **encounter with God**.
English:en.> “El silencio no las separa del mundo,: > “Silence does not separate them from the world; it unites them to it from within.”
English:en.Aunque viven en clausura, **no están des:
Although they live in enclosure, **they are not disconnected**.  
They welcome visitors in the parlor, pray for concrete intentions, and some make products they sell to support their community.  
In a world that runs, they **stop so that love can keep breathing**.
English:en.## Monjas de vida activa: las manos visi: ## Active-life nuns: the visible hands of the Gospel
English:en.Mientras las contemplativas oran en el s:
While contemplatives pray in silence, the **active-life nuns** go out to meet the world.  
They are the ones who **teach, care, accompany, heal and evangelize**.  
Their prayer becomes **action**, their enclosure is the **heart of the neighbor**.
English:en.* En **colegios y universidades**, for: *   In **schools and universities**, forming minds and hearts.
English:en.* En **hospitales**, atendiendo enferm: *   In **hospitals**, tending the sick with tenderness.
English:en.* En **barrios humildes**, compartiend: *   In **humble neighborhoods**, sharing life with the poorest.
English:en.* En **misiones lejanas**, anunciando: *   In **distant missions**, proclaiming Christ with a smile.
English:en.* En **parroquias**, acompañando grupo: *   In **parishes**, accompanying groups, youth, families, the elderly.
English:en.> “Mientras unas oran por el mundo, otra: > “While some pray for the world, others embrace it with their hands. But both love it with the same love.”
English:en.Aunque vivan de formas distintas, **toda:
Although they live in different ways, **all nuns have the same mission**:  
**to follow Christ more closely and make his love present.**  
Some do so from contemplation; others, from action.  
But both are **invisible pillars** that support the body of the Church.
English:en.> “Si la Iglesia es un cuerpo, las monja:
> “If the Church is a body, cloistered nuns are the heart that prays,  
> and active-life nuns are the hands that serve.”
English:en.Las contemplativas recuerdan que Dios es:
Contemplatives remind us that God is the center.  
The active remind us that **God’s love is translated into works**.  
And together they teach us that **faith cannot be understood without prayer or charity**.
English:en.## 💬 ¿Por qué elegir una vida así?: ## 💬 Why choose a life like this?
English:en.Porque en un mundo que busca éxito, ella:
Because in a world that seeks success, they choose **to give their lives**.  
In a time of noise, they **choose silence or service**.  
And in a society that runs without direction, **they stop to look at Christ**.
English:en.Ser monja —de clausura o de vida activa—:
Being a nun —whether cloistered or active— is **a vocation of radical love**:  
a total “yes” to God, a lifelong commitment to the Gospel.
English:en.> “No importa si oran o enseñan, si coci:
> “It doesn’t matter if they pray or teach, if they cook or go on missions:  
> everything in them shouts that God is worth a whole life.”
English:en.En los monasterios o en las calles, \ne:
In monasteries or on the streets,  
in silence or among the shouts of the world,  
**nuns remain witnesses that God is alive**.
English:en.Y mientras el mundo corre buscando senti:
And while the world runs seeking meaning,  
they —with prayer or action— remind us of the deepest secret:  
**happiness lies in giving oneself completely.**
English:en.**Un Ministerio Sagrado al Pueblo de Dio: **A Sacred Ministry to the People of God** _"The faithful expect only one thing from priests: that they be specialists in promoting the encounter between man and God. They are not asked to be experts in economics, construction or politics. They are expected to be experts in spiritual life."_ ~ Pope Benedict XVI
English:en.**¿Podría Dios estar llamándote a ser sa: **Could God be calling you to be a priest?** God made you for a unique purpose. Even before you were born, He knew your vocation, your mission in life. And if you are a faithful Catholic man, God could be calling you to a higher purpose: to become a Catholic priest.
English:en.Los sacerdotes tienen una misión crucial: Priests have a crucial mission: to bring people to Jesus and bring Jesus to people. They are spiritual fathers of thousands of Catholics. They preach the Gospel and offer the sacrifice of the Mass. In short, priests are living witnesses of Christ in the world: men of firm character who stand out in our secular culture.
English:en.Un buen sacerdote es un héroe espiritual: A good priest is a spiritual hero, a man who sacrifices himself for the people of God. Is Jesus calling you to be his priest?
English:en.**El sacerdocio es una vocación.** Crist: **The priesthood is a vocation.** Christ asks some men for the sacrifice of their lives to follow him as his closest companions. From all eternity, certain men are called to the priesthood.
English:en.Es un llamado inscrito en su naturaleza: It is a call inscribed in their nature and, therefore, a call that will bring them fulfillment.
**A priest acts In Persona Christi.** Priests act _in persona Christi capitis_, which means “in the person of Christ, head of the Church”. That is why the priest speaks in the first person at Mass: “This is my body, given for you.”
English:en.Como escribió el Papa Juan Pablo II: _“E: As Pope John Paul II wrote: _“The priest offers his humanity to Christ, so that Christ can use him as an instrument of salvation, making him, so to speak, another Christ.”_
English:en.**Un sacerdote posee un Poder Sagrado.**: **A priest possesses a Sacred Power.** When a priest makes the sacraments present, he possesses a sacred power granted by God, in Latin, _sacra potestas_.
English:en.**El alma de un sacerdote cambia para si: **The soul of a priest changes forever.** In ordination, a man’s soul undergoes an ontological change—a change of being—that marks his soul in an indelible way forever. Once a priest, always a priest.
English:en.El noviazgo es un tiempo para **conocers: Courtship is a time to **get to know each other, relate, and respect one another**. It is not merely a stage before marriage, but an opportunity to learn to love truly. The Church invites living it with depth and joy, because it is the natural path to discern the vocation to conjugal love and prepare for a total and faithful giving.
English:en.## Conocerse: descubrir al otro para ama: ## Getting to know each other: discovering the other to love them better
English:en.El noviazgo es un tiempo de conocimiento: Courtship is a time of mutual knowledge. In it, two people discover each other little by little: their character, their dreams, their faith, their way of facing life. Whoever has been called by God to marriage needs to know well the person with whom they will share their life. The greater the knowledge, the lower the risk of making a mistake.
English:en.Por eso, la Iglesia desea que antes del: Therefore, the Church wishes that before marriage there be a time of courtship, to get to know each other more and thus love each other better. This knowledge is not reduced to external data, but implies discovering the other’s heart: their faith, values, wounds and virtues.
English:en.Amar no es dejarse llevar solo por el se: To love is not to be carried away only by feeling. True love integrates **feeling, intelligence and will**. Feeling ignites, intelligence illuminates and will sustains. Love is not improvised: it is learned, cultivated and decided every day.
English:en.## Tratarse: compartir la vida con since: ## Relating: sharing life with sincerity and faith
English:en.No se puede conocer sin trato, ni amar s: One cannot know without relating, nor love without sharing. The relationship between engaged partners must be deep and sincere, covering essential topics: faith, vision of family, children, work, values… Courtship cannot be based on appearances or passing emotions, but on the search for the truth of the other.
English:en.Los novios cristianos se tratan con resp: Christian couples treat each other with respect and patience, knowing that both are fragile and that love requires forgiveness and understanding. It is not about waiting for the other to change, but about learning to love them as they are, and discerning whether both are walking in the same direction.
English:en.El trato también implica reconocer si ha: The relationship also involves recognizing whether there is **emotional maturity**. Immaturity shows itself when one lives guided by moods, cannot wait, needs attention, or fears commitment. A Christian courtship helps to grow in self-control, to make room for the other, and to cultivate a relationship that is free and sincere.
English:en.## Respetarse: amar con pureza y liberta: ## Respect: love with purity and freedom
English:en.Respetarse es reconocer que el otro es u: Respecting each other means recognizing that the other is a gift, not a possession. Mutual respect is expressed in tenderness, temperance, and chastity. Chastity is not a denial of love, but its noblest defense: it protects the heart and teaches how to love without using the other.
English:en.El Papa Francisco recuerda que el noviaz: Pope Francis reminds us that courtship is “a time of waiting and preparation, which must be lived in the chastity of gestures and words.” That waiting strengthens love, makes it free, mature, and capable of total self-giving. You cannot build a love forever on the pursuit of immediate pleasure.
English:en.Respetarse es también cuidar la comunica: Respecting each other also means taking care of communication, avoiding emotional blackmail, and not putting the other in extreme situations. Authentic love always seeks the good of the beloved, not one’s own satisfaction. Thus one learns to love as Christ loved: with patience, with self-giving, and without expecting anything in return.
English:en.Podemos decir que el amor humano tiene t: We can say that human love has three phases, which do not replace one another but integrate:
English:en.1. **Atracción:** surge espontáneamente: 1.  **Attraction:** arises spontaneously. Someone seems attractive to you; interest and the desire to get to know them are born.
English:en.2. **Enamoramiento:** los sentimientos: 2.  **Falling in love:** feelings are on edge. One enjoys the presence of the other and dreams of a future together.
English:en.3. **Amor decidido:** es la fase más ma: 3.  **Decided love:** is the most mature phase. Loving is no longer just feeling, but **choosing to love**: deciding to do so every day, even when it is difficult.
English:en.El sentimiento no se elige, pero el amor: You do not choose feelings, but you do choose love. To love is a decision that involves sacrifice, fidelity, and will. When one loves this way, the feeling returns stronger and deeper, because gratuitous love — given without expecting anything in return — generates joy and fullness.
English:en.El noviazgo cristiano es un camino para: Christian courtship is a path to learn to love like Christ: with freedom, tenderness, and self-giving. It is not about seeking perfection, but about walking together toward it, supported by the grace of God.
English:en.Vivir un noviazgo así es preparar los ci:
Living such a courtship is preparing the foundations of a solid marriage. As Pope Francis says, “coexistence is an art, a patient, beautiful and fascinating path that has rules summed up in three words: May I?, Thank you, Forgive.”  
Three words that also sum up a holy courtship: respect, gratitude, and constant reconciliation.
English:en.**Ora et labora** —reza y trabaja—. \nE:
**Ora et labora** —pray and work—.  
That is the formula that summarizes the whole life of the monk. But behind those three words there is a world: a way of life centered on **the search for God**, on the silence of the monastery, and on the peace of a routine offered as prayer.
English:en.El **monje** vive para **contemplar a Di:
The **monk** lives to **contemplate God**. He does not flee the world, but embraces it from the heart, interceding for the needs of all people.  
Each day, his prayer invisibly sustains the Church.  
His vocation is **contemplative**, but not useless: monks draw grace upon the world with their silent fidelity.
English:en.### El ritmo del día: oración, lectura y: ### The rhythm of the day: prayer, reading and work
English:en.El día del monje gira como un reloj sagr: The monk’s day revolves like a sacred clock around three pillars:
English:en.1. **Oración** – comunitaria y personal:
1.  **Prayer** – communal and personal.  
    The monks pray the **Divine Office**, the liturgical “hours” that mark the day:
English:en.Y en el centro de todo: la **Eucaristía*: And at the center of it all: the **Eucharist**, the living heart of the monastery.
English:en.2. **Lectio divina** – la lectura orant:
2.  **Lectio divina** – the prayerful reading of the Word.  
    It is not academic study, but **listening to the Spirit**. From it sprang the great Benedictine libraries that preserved Christian and Greco-Roman culture for centuries.
English:en.3. **Trabajo** – manual o intelectual,:
3.  **Work** – manual or intellectual, always offered to God.  
    In an abbey there can be bakers, shoemakers, gardeners, bookbinders, musicians, librarians or teachers.  
    Everything is done in obedience, in silence and with love.
English:en.### Ora et labora: una oración hecha tra: ### Ora et labora: prayer made work
English:en.En el monasterio **no hay horas vacías**:
In the monastery **there are no idle hours**. Everything — singing the psalms, repairing a shoe or copying a book — is a form of prayer.  
Work supports the monastery and enables works of charity.  
The balance between prayer, work and study keeps the monk **in peace, serene and centered on God**.
English:en.De la atención amorosa a la **lectio div:
From the loving attention to **lectio divina**, monks naturally turned to **study**.  
Therefore, medieval abbeys were **beacons of light** in dark times:  
they copied manuscripts, taught people to read and sowed the foundations of European culture.
English:en.Aunque “monje” viene del griego _monos_:
Although “monk” comes from the Greek _monos_ (alone), the monk **does not live isolated**, but **in community**.  
Under the guidance of an abbot, all seek “**to have one heart and one soul in God**”, as St. Augustine says.  
The monastery is a family where each brother helps the other to reach heaven.
English:en.Los **monjes** viven según la **Regla de:
**Monks** live according to the **Rule of Saint Benedict**, centered on contemplation.  
**Friars** (Franciscans, Dominicans, Carmelites…) also consecrated, go out into the world to preach and serve.  
And **religious clerics** (like the Jesuits) dedicate their lives to apostolate and teaching.  
Each path is different, but all seek the same: **God in all things**.
English:en.### En palabras de San Benito: ### In the words of Saint Benedict
> “Put nothing before the love of Christ.”  
> — _Rule of Saint Benedict, ch. 4_
English:en.**Los sacerdotes hacen mucho más que cel:
**Priests do much more than celebrate Mass and pray all day.**  
The life of a priest is active, demanding, challenging… and deeply rewarding.
English:en.Existen muchos ministerios especializado: There are many specialized ministries, such as being a chaplain, working in archdiocesan offices, or teaching in a seminary. But most priests serve in parishes.
English:en.La gran mayoría de los sacerdotes viven: The vast majority of priests live happy and fulfilling lives. They love the people they serve and, in turn, are loved by their parishioners. Traditionally, priests are understood to fulfill the biblical roles of **priest, prophet and king.**
English:en.Los sacerdotes instruyen a otros en la f: Priests instruct others in the faith.
English:en.Los sacerdotes guían, unen y animan a su: Priests guide, unite and encourage their parishioners.
English:en.Los sacerdotes administran los sacrament: Priests administer the sacraments and foster holiness.
English:en.* Celebrar la Misa y predicar el Evang: *   Celebrating Mass and preaching the Gospel.
English:en.* Incorporar nuevos miembros a la Igle: *   Bringing new members into the Church through Baptism.
English:en.* Escuchar confesiones y ofrecer direc: *   Hearing confessions and offering spiritual direction.
English:en.* Ayudar a adolescentes y jóvenes adul: *   Helping adolescents and young adults to know Christ.
English:en.* Preparar a las parejas para el matri: *   Preparing couples for marriage and accompanying them in their married life.
English:en.* Alimentar a los pobres, visitar cárc: *   Feeding the poor, visiting prisons and promoting justice.
English:en.* Acompañar a quienes pasan por moment: *   Accompanying those going through difficult times.
English:en.* Visitar a los enfermos en los hospit: *   Visiting the sick in hospitals and anointing them for healing.
English:en.* Celebrar funerales y dar sepultura a: *   Celebrating funerals and burying the dead.
English:en.* Administrar los asuntos materiales d: *   Managing the material affairs of the parish.
English:en.* Orar diariamente por el Pueblo de Di: *   Praying daily for the People of God.
English:en.Relaciones antes del matrimonio: amar si: Relationships before marriage: loving without possessing
English:en.## Relaciones antes del matrimonio: amar: ## Relationships before marriage: loving without possessing
English:en.El amor no se mide por la intensidad del:
Love is not measured by the intensity of desire, but by the truth of self-giving.  
In a time that confuses using with loving, and passion with happiness, many hearts end up broken because they skip God’s plan. Not because He wants to deprive us of something, but because He loves us so much that He only wants to give us what truly makes us free, clean, and happy.
English:en.Muchos piensan que el amor es tener al o: Many think love is having the other, making them theirs, merging as much as possible. But Christian love does not seek to possess, but to **give and care**. Wanting is wanting for myself; loving is wanting the good of the other, even above my own desires.
English:en.Cuando una relación se vuelve posesiva,: When a relationship becomes possessive, when jealousy, control or distrust appear, something has gone wrong. The human heart was made to love in freedom, and where there is fear or domination, love withers.
English:en.Los celos son muchas veces la señal de u: Jealousy is often a sign of a relationship that has lost its purity or balance: because the body was given before the soul, or because love was confused with dependence. Loving well requires learning to **wait, respect and trust**.
English:en.## El amor se destruye cuando se adelant: ## Love is destroyed when it is rushed
English:en.La sexualidad es un don precioso de Dios: Sexuality is a precious gift from God, but it has its place: marriage. Not because pleasure is bad, but because the body has a language that says “I give myself completely, forever.” When that promise is spoken before the soul is ready, without being sealed before God, something breaks inside.
English:en.**El sexo antes del matrimonio no une: c:
**Sex before marriage does not unite: it confuses.**  
It makes one believe there is intimacy where there is not yet, and leaves wounds that can last for years: feelings of emptiness, pain, dependence or distrust.
English:en.El cuerpo se entrega antes de que la vol: The body is given before the will is mature, and then the soul rebels, because it was created for a total and definitive union. That is why so many relationships wear out, fade, or become torment.
English:en.Donde hay pecado, hay sufrimiento. No co: Where there is sin, there is suffering. Not as punishment, but as consequence. Because love is made for the light, not for the darkness.
English:en.## La castidad: la gran escuela del amor: ## Chastity: the great school of love
English:en.Ser casto no es reprimir el amor, sino *: Being chaste is not repressing love, but **learning to love truly**. Chastity orders the heart so that love is pure, joyful and faithful.
English:en.Los novios que luchan por la pureza no v: Fiancés who strive for purity do not live less love: they live it better. Their affection is stronger, their joy purer, their trust more solid. There are no shadows, no fear, no shame.
English:en.Como enseña el Catecismo de la Iglesia C: As the Catechism of the Catholic Church teaches:
English:en.> “Los novios están llamados a vivir la: "> “The engaged are called to live chastity in continence. In this trial they must see a discovery of mutual respect and a learning of fidelity. They will reserve for marriage the expressions of tenderness proper to conjugal love.”
English:en.Cada esfuerzo, cada renuncia, cada vez q: Every effort, every renunciation, every time one says “no” to impulse and “yes” to God, plants a seed that will bear fruit in the future marriage. **You reap what you sow.**
English:en.El respeto es el guardián de la felicida: Respect is the guardian of spouses’ happiness. The cleaner they arrive at the altar, the deeper their union. Those who have lived it say so: engaged couples who conquer themselves and keep themselves arrive with renewed excitement, freshness and tenderness.
English:en.La pasión tiene su lugar, pero cuando se:
Passion has its place, but when used without restraint, it ends up tiring. **Nothing used without measure remains beautiful.**  
Therefore, learning to wait is the best investment in love.
English:en.El noviazgo no es un matrimonio en peque: Courtship is not a small marriage. There is still no right to total giving. It is a time to get to know each other, to grow together, to prepare the soul and the heart.
English:en.El amor no necesita probarse con el cuer: Love does not need to be proven with the body, but shown with fidelity, respect, care and prayer. Whoever truly loves does not pressure. Whoever loves, waits.
English:en.Si uno de los dos no está viviendo su fe: If one of the two is not living their faith or does not understand what it means to be a child of God, one must help them with patience, but also with firmness. Loving is not allowing what destroys, but **inviting the other to the best of themselves**.
English:en.Puede que necesitéis un tiempo de distan: You may need some time apart, to pray, clarify feelings and heal. That’s okay. If love is true, it will move forward; if not, it is better to let it go before losing peace.
English:en.Y si necesitáis luz, **buscad consejo en: And if you need guidance, **seek counsel from a good priest**. Confess, pray together, receive the sacraments. With God’s grace, everything is possible. Without it, nothing endures.
English:en.Vivir la pureza también pasa por la form: Living purity also involves the way you present yourself. It is not about covering up or hiding, but dressing with elegance, modesty, and respect for oneself and the other. Beauty lies in dignity, not in provocation.
English:en.Una mirada, un gesto, una palabra pueden: A look, a gesture, a word can ignite passions that should not burn. That is why one must be prudent. Avoid lonely places, ambiguous moments, dark environments. Light protects love.
English:en.## Si te cuesta, no te rindas: ## If it’s hard, don’t give up
English:en.Ser puro no es fácil, pero es posible. R: Being pure is not easy, but it is possible. It requires will, prayer and the sacraments. And the reward is great: an inner peace that no pleasure can equal.
English:en.Hay novios que lo consiguen. Muchos. Que: There are engaged couples who manage it. Many. Who live their love with respect and joy, and who arrive at marriage with a clean happiness. They are testimony that **purity does not take away love: it elevates it**.
English:en.Y si has caído, **no te quedes ahí**. Di: And if you have fallen, **don’t stay there**. God never tires of forgiving. Start again, trust, and let his mercy renew your heart.
English:en.Tu novio no es todavía tu esposo. El amo: Your boyfriend is not yet your husband. Total love belongs to marriage. Don’t be fooled by those who tell you “it doesn’t matter,” that “everyone does it.” Loving with purity is swimming against the current, but those who do so find true joy.
English:en.Defiende tu castidad con entereza. Haz d: Defend your chastity with firmness. Make your love story a beautiful and clean testimony, something you can one day tell your children without shame, with a heart full of gratitude.
Your purity is not fragility, it is strength.  
Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, not an instrument of desire.  
Your soul is for God.
English:en.Y recuerda: **más vale entrar sola en el: And remember: **better to enter the Kingdom of Heaven alone than accompanied on the wrong path.**
English:en.## María, modelo de pureza y ternura: ## Mary, model of purity and tenderness
English:en.Mira a María, Virgen y Madre. En Ella se: Look to Mary, Virgin and Mother. In Her delicacy and strength, tenderness and firmness come together. Mary teaches that purity is not coldness, but true love.
English:en.Su ejemplo ha sostenido a generaciones e: Her example has sustained entire generations of young people who chose to love well, at all costs. Also look to the saints who defended their purity with courage: Maria Goretti, Josefina Vilaseca… They are proof that it is worth it.
English:en.¡La mejor formación que ofrece la Iglesi: The best formation the Church offers!
English:en.El **seminario** es el lugar donde un ho:
The **seminary** is the place where a man is formed —mind, body and soul— in the image of **Jesus Christ**.  
It is not a place where seminarians walk in silence all day singing in Latin; on the contrary, it is a **place of joy, fraternity and deep learning**.  
Today’s seminarians receive the best formation the Church offers!
English:en.> “La formación de los futuros sacerdote:
"> “The formation of future priests… is considered by the Church as one of the most demanding and important tasks for the future of the evangelization of humanity.”  
> — _St. John Paul II, Pastores Dabo Vobis_
English:en.¿Ser laico es una vocación?: Is being a layperson a vocation?
English:en.### **El Pueblo de Dios y la Vocación La: ### **The People of God and the Lay Vocation**
English:en.El **Pueblo de Dios** está compuesto, en: The **People of God** is made up, for the most part, of **lay faithful**: all the **baptized who have not received the sacrament of Holy Orders nor taken religious vows**. Christ calls them as **Church**, not only to be recipients of the Good News of Salvation, but also to be **active agents of evangelization** in the world. Each baptized person is invited to sow the Gospel in God’s “vineyard,” which is the society in which they live, carrying out an **indispensable evangelizing task**.
English:en.Como nos recuerda el Señor en el Evangel: As the Lord reminds us in the Gospel:
English:en.> “Id también vosotros a mi viña” (Mt. 2:
"> “You also go into my vineyard” (Mt. 20:3-4)  
> “Go into all the world and proclaim the Good News to all creation” (Mk. 16:15; cf. ChL 33)
English:en.A través del **Bautismo**, los fieles so: Through **Baptism**, the faithful are **grafted into Christ** and receive a **threefold vocation**:
English:en.1. **Sacerdotal**: ofrecer la propia vi: 1.  **Priestly**: to offer one’s life as a spiritual sacrifice, sanctifying daily life through acts of love and service.
English:en.2. **Profética**: ser testigos de la ve: 2.  **Prophetic**: to be witnesses of Christ’s truth in words and actions, proclaiming the Gospel coherently in all areas of life.
English:en.3. **Real**: participar en la construcc: 3.  **Kingly**: to participate in building society according to the values of the Kingdom of God, being a leaven of justice and peace in public life.
English:en.Según **Lumen Gentium**, los laicos está: According to **Lumen Gentium**, the laity are called to **seek the Kingdom of God in their daily lives**, ordering temporal affairs according to the spirit of Jesus Christ. They act as **“yeast” that sanctifies the world from within**, participating in the mission of the Church in **social, family and professional** life. This vocation **must be constantly fostered** by pastors in particular Churches, helping laypeople to discover their identity and mission in the world.
English:en.Cada laico está llamado a **transformar: Each lay person is called to **transform their surroundings**, bringing the faith to all dimensions of life:
English:en.* En el **trabajo**, siendo testimonio: *   At **work**, being a witness of honesty, excellence and service.
English:en.* En la **política y la economía**, pr: *   In **politics and the economy**, promoting justice, solidarity and the common good.
English:en.* En la **ciencia, el arte y la cultur: *   In **science, art and culture**, illuminating creativity with Christian values.
English:en.* En la **familia y la comunidad**, se: *   In **family and community**, sowing love, respect and fraternity.
English:en.Ser laico no es secundario ni pasivo; es: Being lay is not secondary or passive; it is **an active and concrete vocation** that requires formation, prayer and commitment. Each Christian, in daily life, is called to **be a sign of the Kingdom of God in the world**, fulfilling their mission of evangelization from their own reality and exercising their threefold function **priestly, prophetic and kingly**, as Lumen Gentium teaches.
English:en.## **¿Cómo saber si Dios me está llamand: ## **How to know if God is calling me?**
English:en.Si alguna vez has pensado en ser sacerdo: If you have ever thought about becoming a priest, these signs can help you discover whether God is calling you to follow him more closely:
English:en.### **2\\. Dios ha puesto en tu corazón: ### **2. God has placed in your heart the desire to be a priest.**
English:en.Tal vez no sabes de dónde viene, pero la:
Maybe you don’t know where it comes from, but the idea of being a priest often crosses your mind.  
Sometimes you set it aside, other times it strongly attracts you… but it never completely disappears.  
That constant restlessness can be a seed that God has planted in your heart.  
Talk about it! With a priest you admire or with someone you know will help you and tell them what you feel.
English:en.### **2\\. Sientes un gran amor por Cris: ### **2. You feel a great love for Christ, for the Church and for her teaching.**
English:en.Te entusiasma conocer más sobre la fe, l:
You are eager to learn more about the faith, to read about the saints, doctrine or the life of the Church.  
You are attracted to the different vocations and charisms, and it excites you to see how all serve the same Lord.  
A man called to the priesthood usually feels at home within the Church and enjoys learning “all things Catholic.”
English:en.### **3\\. Otras personas te han dicho q: ### **3. Other people have told you that you would make a good priest.**
English:en.A veces los demás ven algo en ti que tú:
Sometimes others see something in you that you yourself do not notice.  
When someone says to you, “Have you thought about becoming a priest? I think you would be a good one,”  
it can be a way God speaks to you through them.  
Many priests say that after hearing that comment repeatedly, they decided to take the step toward the seminary.
English:en.### **4\\. Deseas vivir una vida de orac: ### **4. You desire to live a life of prayer and grow in virtue.**
English:en.El Papa Benedicto XVI decía que lo que s:
Pope Benedict XVI said that what is expected of a priest is that he be an expert in spiritual life.  
Therefore, one who feels the call seeks to attend Mass, pray frequently, confess, serve others and grow inwardly.
English:en.### **5\\. Quieres ayudar a los demás a: ### **5. You want to help others draw closer to Jesus.**
English:en.El sacerdote lleva a Jesús a las persona:
The priest brings Jesus to people and people to Jesus.  
If you feel in your heart the desire to accompany, teach, console or guide others in their faith,  
it may be that God is calling you to serve as a priest.  
The priestly vocation consists, ultimately, in **leading others to heaven.**
English:en.Si has pensado en el sacerdocio, pero no:
If you have considered the priesthood but do not see yourself with all these qualities, **do not worry.**  
No one is born a priest: one becomes a priest with God’s help and the formation the Church offers.
English:en.Habla con tu **Director espiritual** o c:
Talk with your **spiritual director** or with a priest you trust.  
They can help you discern more clearly what God is asking of you.  
And remember: true happiness and peace are found **only by following God’s will.**
English:en.Si Él te llama, **su gracia te llevará h: If He calls you, **his grace will carry you to the end.**
English:en.# La Vida Activa: servir al mundo desde: # The Active Life: serving the world through total self-giving to God
